title: Window and Door Rebates in Burnaby 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: Burnaby homes outside the City of Vancouver can claim $100 per window or door. 53% of households live in apartments, so check first whether your home is eligible.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Burnaby
lead: Burnaby borders Vancouver, but the rebate rules change at the city line. A Burnaby house can claim $100 per window, while a house a few blocks west cannot. The bigger question here is whether you live in a house at all, because 53% of Burnaby households live in apartments.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Burnaby
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists $100 per opening for its gas customers, except in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Burnaby bungalow

A bungalow with 11 windows, a patio door and a front door is 13 openings. That pays 13 x $100 = $1,300. The same house across the boundary in Vancouver would earn nothing from this program.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 101,135 households in Burnaby. About 35,865 (35%) live in homes built before 1981, but 53% live in apartments and 40% rent, so only 9,220 are owner-occupied detached houses from that era. BC Hydro's home rebate does not cover condo or apartment units. Owners of a unit in a tower or townhouse complex should ask about BC Hydro's Condo and Apartment Rebate Program. Townhouses with their own meters and an account not held by a strata corporation can qualify.

Burnaby's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was 1.1°C, and the coldest day was -16.2°C. Winters are damp. Condensation on old windows is often the main complaint, and a window with a low U-factor keeps the inside glass warmer. That helps with mould as well as comfort.

Eligible windows and doors must carry a certification from CSA, Intertek, Labtest, QAI or NFRC, and reach a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower. They must replace existing units that separate a heated space from the outdoors or an unheated space. Skylights do not count. Ask each contractor to put the model and U-factor on the quote, and read the label when the units arrive.

BC Hydro needs the invoice and a photo of the manufacturer label on every window and door you claim. Its checklist and sample invoice are on the program page. Take the photos on installation day. Missing labels are the most common reason a window claim stalls, since labels are hard to reach after trim goes on.

The rebate needs a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, and lower means less heat loss. Many window labels show the older imperial scale instead. To convert, multiply the imperial number by 5.678. A label that says U-0.30 equals 1.70 W/m2-K, which is too high. A label that says U-0.21 equals about 1.19 W/m2-K and passes. Ask the contractor to quote the metric value for each model so you do not have to convert.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_steps: Confirm you live in a house, row home or duplex with its own meter, not a condo.
Collect quotes that list the U-factor of every window and door.
Photograph each label on installation day.
Keep the invoice and apply within six months.
Add insulation or a water heater to the same application to check the bonus.
faq: I live in a Burnaby condo. Can I claim?
Not under this program. BC Hydro has a separate Condo and Apartment Rebate Program.
How is Burnaby different from Vancouver?
Homes inside the City of Vancouver are excluded from the Tier 2 window rebate. Burnaby homes are not.
How many windows can I claim?
Up to 20 openings at $100 each, for a $2,000 cap.
Can a contractor claim for me?
The account holder applies. A contractor can help gather documents.
